title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools (2026)
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood's core People Ops guidance for new and existing employees: how we think about working at Redwood, our role and career ladder structure, benefits and perks, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and a reference to the primary internal tools used day-to-day. This document is intended for all employees and hiring managers.

--

## 1. Working at Redwood (short intro)

Redwood is a developer-first company building infrastructure for production LLM inference. Our people principles emphasize ownership, experimental rigor, reliable delivery, and empathy for users and teammates. Expectations for behaviour include:

- Ship: prioritize outcomes and iterate quickly.
- Communicate: keep teams and stakeholders informed; use asynchronous updates in Confluence and Slack summaries for major changes.
- Respect: seek diverse perspectives and give constructive feedback.
- Reliability: design for production and document operational assumptions.

Ownership and clarity: each service or project should have a documented owner, an SLA or success metric, and a short runbook linked from the team wiki.

## 2. Roles & Career Ladders

Redwood maintains role ladders for major functions to set expectations for impact, scope, and growth. Below are compact summaries — see the linked role profiles for full competencies and promotion criteria.

Role ladder summary (engineers and product examples):

| Level | Common title | Typical years | Key expectations |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| IC1 | Software Engineer I | 0-2 yrs | Contributes to tasks, follows designs, owns small features, writes tests. |
| IC2 | Software Engineer II | 2-5 yrs | Owns components, mentors interns, improves code health, reliably delivers medium-sized features. |
| IC3 | Senior Software Engineer | 5+ yrs | Leads complex projects, designs systems, influences roadmap, mentors broadly. |
| IC4 | Staff Engineer | 7+ yrs | Technical leadership across teams, sets architecture, drives cross-team initiatives. |
| IC5 | Principal Engineer | 10+ yrs | Company-level technical strategy, long-term architecture, deep domain expertise. |

Product ladder summary:

- PM1 (Associate PM): supports features, writes PRDs with clear metrics.
- PM2 (Product Manager): owns a product area or major feature set end-to-end.
- PM3 (Senior PM): defines multi-quarter strategy, leads cross-functional programs.
- PM4 (Director of Product): leads multiple product teams, influences company strategy.

Expectations and promotion process (high level):

1. Demonstrated impact over multiple quarters aligned to role competencies.
2. Peer and manager feedback; reviewers include cross-functional partners.
3. Submission of evidence packet (projects, metrics, mentoring examples) to People Ops.
4. Calibration committee review and final decision.

Owners for ladder maintenance: People Ops (owner), Eng Leadership (engineering ladders), Product Leadership (product ladders).

## 3. Benefits & Perks (summary)

Redwood offers a competitive benefits package intended to support health, family, growth, and well-being. Highlights: 

Health & financial
- Medical, dental, and vision plans for employees and dependents (US and equivalent regional plans in EMEA/APAC).
- 401(k) / pension matching where applicable.
- Equity grants for full-time employees with standard vesting (4 years, 1-year cliff unless otherwise specified in offer).

Leave & flexibility
- Generous paid time off (PTO) policy: flexible vacation + public holidays by region.
- Parental leave: primary and secondary caregiver policies; short-term disability where applicable.
- Flexible remote/hybrid work policy (region-specific guidelines documented in People Ops pages).

Development & learning
- Annual professional development stipend (e.g., conference + training allowances).
- Internal learning stipend for certifications and coursework.
- Regular brown-bags, tech talks, and an internal mentorship program.

Wellness & office perks
- Mental health support and EAP.
- Commuter benefits and flexible office stipends.
- Team offsites and monthly social budgets.

Compensation philosophy: market-competitive base, role-leveled bands, equity to align long-term incentives, and annual compensation review cycles. For detailed plan summaries, eligibility, and region-specific rules, see linked benefits pages in the People Ops space.

## 4. Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Principles of hiring
- Hire for mission, cognitive ability, and role fit.
- Structured interviews with rubrics to reduce bias.
- Fast but thoughtful process: aim for clarity and timely feedback at every stage.

Typical hiring steps (candidate journey)
1. Sourcing / application review.
2. Recruiter screen (role fit, compensation expectations, basic logistics).
3. Manager or technical screen (30-45 min).
4. Onsite / loop: 3-5 interviews covering system design, coding/technical depth, product sense (for PMs), and culture fit.
5. Debrief and hire/no-hire decision.
6. Offer, background check, and onboarding scheduling.

Hiring manager checklist (pre-offer)
- Confirm hiring rubric and interviewers.
- Write clear role brief and success metrics for first 6 months.
- Budget and compensation alignment with Finance.

Onboarding: first 90 days (owner and checkpoints)

Week 0 (before start)
- HR sends welcome packet, equipment survey, and first-week schedule. (Owner: People Ops)

Week 1: Setup and orientation
1. Day 1: Company orientation and benefits walkthrough (People Ops).
2. Team orientation: meet direct manager, buddy introduction, role expectations, team priorities. (Owner: hiring manager)
3. Access: GitHub, Confluence, Slack, CI/CD, internal registries, dev cluster credentials. (Owner: Eng IT / Oncall team)

Weeks 2-4: Ramp and early deliverables
- Small onboarding tickets (first code/PR for engineers, first customer problem or requirement doc for PMs).
- 1:1 cadence established (weekly with manager, biweekly with buddy).
- Security and compliance training completed.

30-90 days: Impact and calibration
- Deliver first owned scope (bugfix or feature).
- Draft a 90-day plan and present to manager.
- Skip-level with manager and cross-functional partners for alignment.

Onboarding artifacts checklist (required completion within 30 days):
- Completed Confluence onboarding checklist page (link to team page).
- Two completed training modules (security + product compliance).
- First PR merged and paired review.

Promotion of psychological safety: managers should schedule a 1:1 onboarding feedback session at day 14 and day 60.

## 5. Internal Tools Guide (concise reference)

This section lists the primary internal tools, purpose, and quick links. Teams should keep the team wiki updated with service-specific runbooks and CI links.

- Confluence (this space): canonical policies, runbooks, design docs, onboarding checklists. Always add an owner and "last updated" date to new pages.
- Slack: primary communication channel. Use structured channels (#eng-infra, #product-announcements, team channels). Use threads to keep discussions organized.
- GitHub: source of truth for code. Use protected branches, required reviews, and CI checks.
- Jira: issue tracking and sprint planning for product and engineering teams.
- CI/CD (internal runner + GitHub Actions): deployment pipelines and release tags. Release notes should be posted to Confluence release pages and #releases channel.
- Redwood Console (internal): observability dashboard, route/model cost/latency metrics, and rollout control plane for Dedicated/Private customers. Operational alerts originated here should link to runbooks.
- Identity & Access (Okta / SSO): central authentication and application provisioning. Use access requests for additional role-based permissions.
- Cloud Console (GCP/AWS): infra resource view; use least privilege IAM, request access via infra Slack channel and follow change-management templates.
- Internal CLI tools: a short list of common commands is maintained on the eng-developer-experience wiki (dev-tools clis, credential helpers).

Tools etiquette and responsibilities:
- Keep channels focused: use #team triage channel for urgent incidents, #ops for operational coordination.
- Document changes: any system config changes must be accompanied by a Confluence change entry and brief in #infra-changes.
- Security: do not share secrets in Slack; use the secrets manager and documented rotation policies.

## 6. Manager & Hiring Manager Playbook (quick reference)

- Prepare a 30/60/90 plan with measurable deliverables before new hire starts.
- Assign a peer buddy for the first 90 days (responsibilities: context, codewalk, social introduction).
- Run monthly calibration reviews for career development and performance.

## 7. Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

Q: Who do I contact for benefits questions?
A: People Ops benefits team; open a ticket via the People Ops portal or email people-ops@redwood.example.com.

Q: Where do I find the on-call runbooks?
A: Team runbooks are linked from each service page in Confluence (see eng-sre > runbooks). For urgent incidents, follow the oncall escalation playbook.

Q: How do I request additional hardware or cloud quota?
A: File a request in #infra-requests and attach the quota request form; include projected monthly usage and justification.
